TextView.android:text: Notice where your attention is, and gently bring it back when it wanders. You don't need to empty your mind or force calm. Returning IS the practice.
Build attention and begin the day with intention. Focus gently on breath or sounds.
Take a 2–3 minute pause during a break to reconnect with 5-4-3-2-1 Grounding.
Wind down with a gentle body scan. Dim screen mode with quiet, soft ending.
Start gently. If three sessions feel like too much, keep the morning session and treat others as optional. Missing a day is normal; simply begin again when you can.
Select a practice that fits how you feel right now. No need to empty your mind.
Feel one natural breath. When your mind wanders, gently acknowledge: 'thinking', and return.
Reconnect with the present when your mind feels busy. Name 5 see, 4 feel, 3 hear, 2 smell, 1 taste.
Make room for what is here without needing to fix it immediately. Notice thoughts, sounds, sensations.
Count each exhale from 1 to 5. If you lose count, simply begin again at 1 without judgment.
Repeat gentle warmth: 'May I be kind to myself', 'May I have patience', 'May I find moments of ease'.
Release held tension from feet to face. Dim screen mode with quiet, unhurried fade-out.
Practice attention when sitting still doesn't feel right. Notice feet lifting, moving, and touching ground.
Lectio Divina: Read slowly, savor the Word of God, and abide in Christ's peace.
These durations are suggestions, not requirements. Stay at any stage longer if it feels comfortable.
Morning: 3m Breath • Afternoon: 2m Grounding • Night: 3–5m Body Scan
Learn the basic cycle: Notice ➔ Become distracted ➔ Notice the distraction ➔ Gently return. Returning is not a mistake; returning is the practice.
Morning: 5m Breath/Sound • Afternoon: 3m Grounding/Walking • Night: 5m Body Scan
When a thought appears, don't battle it. Silently name it “thinking” or “planning,” then return to your chosen point of attention.
Morning: 5–7m Attention • Afternoon: 3–5m from Needs • Night: 5–7m Sleep
Try different anchors—breath, sounds, feet on the floor—and notice which feel comfortable. Anchor flexibility protects you from strain.
Morning: 5–10m Preferred • Afternoon: 3–5m Need • Night: 5–10m Sleep
At the end of the week, keep the practices and lengths you can realistically enjoy. Longer isn’t automatically better.

Meditation doesn’t feel helpful for everyone; sometimes it can increase distress. If a practice makes you feel worse, stop, open your eyes, and orient yourself to the room or do something comforting. Meditation can complement care, but it shouldn’t replace qualified professional support (NCCIH / NHS guidance).
Consistency is showing up when you can. Missed days are completely normal—never treated as failure.
